papers.title: Caesarean section in Bangladesh, 2012-13 to 2025: facility birth, the private sector and small-area geography
papers.abstract: Background: In Bangladesh, caesarean section rose from one in five births in 2012-13 to one in two in 2025. We asked how much of this rise came from more facility births, a move to private facilities, and changing rates within sectors. Methods: This repeated cross-sectional study used Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys from 2012-13, 2019 and 2025 (26,539 recent mothers). A Kitagawa decomposition split the rise into parts. For 2025, we mapped caesarean use among facility births in 2,720 clusters and examined modelled travel time. Results: The caesarean rate rose from 19.5% (95% CI 18.1 to 20.9) to 52.0% (50.7 to 53.2). More facility births made up 82.8% (78.9 to 87.7) of this 32.5 point rise and the move to private facilities 12.6% (10.1 to 15.0). In a one-step version, place of birth made up 94.7% (90.7 to 98.9). The private caesarean rate rose from 79.1% to 86.1%, while the public rate fell from 38.7% to 33.5%. Among private first births, which rarely follow a previous caesarean, the 2025 rate was 4.8 points (0.3 to 10.2) above the 2012-13 model's prediction. The 2025 private rate was 85% to 87% in every wealth group. Longer travel time was linked with fewer caesareans, mainly through fewer facility births. Among private-sector births, travel time was not linked with caesarean (prevalence ratio 0.99 per 10 minutes, 0.97 to 1.01). Caesarean use among facility births clustered geographically; the private share of births in nearby clusters, not household factors, accounted for much of this. Conclusions: In accounting terms, most of the rise came from births moving into facilities, mostly private ones, where caesarean was already common. The data cannot show how many caesareans were needed. If 2025 sector mix and rates persist, more facility births would keep raising the national rate.

papers.title: A clinical audit of postoperative care after emergency caesarean section for obstructed labour at a national referral hospital in Uganda
papers.abstract: Background Postoperative complications after emergency caesarean section (C/S) due to obstructed labour (O/L) are a significant contributing factor to maternal morbidity in low-resource settings. At Kawempe National Referral Hospital (KNRH) in Kampala, Uganda, hospital records from late 2024 showed an overall adverse outcome rate of approximately 10% among all women delivered by caesarean section, with postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) and surgical site infection (SSI) among the recorded outcomes. Women who deliver by C/S for O/L are particularly a high-risk group, yet adherence to postoperative care standards in this group had not been systematically evaluated. This audit therefore aimed at assessing whether a clinical audit could improve the quality of postoperative care among women undergoing C/S for O/L. Methods A criterion-based audit cycle was conducted at a national referral hospital in Kampala, Uganda, over six months. At baseline, 150 case files of mothers who delivered by caesarean section due to O/L were reviewed retrospectively, and care practices were evaluated against six care standards derived from World Health Organisation (WHO) and Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) guidelines. These included: monitoring of vital signs (blood pressure, pulse rate, respiratory rate, temperature, oxygen saturation), administration of analgesia, surgical site care, administration of prophylactic and empirical antibiotics, monitoring for postpartum haemorrhage (monitoring uterine tone and vaginal bleeding), and bladder care. Findings were shared with stakeholders, and gaps were identified. Interventions such as continuous medical education (CME) sessions, protocol dissemination, and workflow adjustments, co-developed with stakeholders, were rigorously implemented for 2 months and 2 weeks. An endline audit was done by reviewing 149 case files. Data analysis involved a comparative description of the baseline and endline audits to determine statistical significance using a chi-square test. To assess the overall level of adherence to postoperative care standards, a composite indicator overall mean care score was computed for both baseline and endline phases. This metric was derived by aggregating compliance across all evaluated components of the standards. Results Statistically significant improvements were noted in three standards: Antibiotic administration-prophylactic antibiotics administration (38.0% to 60.4%; p<0.001) and empiric antibiotics administration on Day 1(metronidazole-13.7% to 96.2%, p<0.001), urine output monitoring on Day 1(17.3% to 28.9%; p=0.012), and analgesia administration (paracetamol and rectal diclofenac- 50% to above 80%, p<0.002). However, critical gaps persisted, with no observed improvement in vital sign monitoring and surgical site care, and a paradoxical decline in uterine tone monitoring (90.0 to 88.7%; p=0.667). The overall mean care score improved from 46.7% at baseline to 61.1% at endline (absolute increase of +14.4% points). Conclusion The results of this study show that a clinical audit is a feasible quality improvement tool that can enhance postoperative care for mothers who deliver by C/S due to O/L in low-resource settings. However, there is a need to evaluate the other standards that did not have an improvement.

papers.title: Maternal epigenetic age acceleration in early pregnancy, gestational duration, and spontaneous preterm birth among Black women in the NuMom2b study
papers.abstract: Importance: Preterm birth is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality and disproportionately affects Black birthing people in the United States. DNA methylation based measures of biological aging may capture physiologic dysregulation relevant to birth timing. We aim to determine whether maternal epigenetic age acceleration in early pregnancy is associated with gestational duration, spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB), and small for gestational age (SGA) among Black nulliparous pregnant individuals. Methods: This is a secondary data analysis of the prospective, multicenter Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-Be (nuMoM2b). Participants enrolled in eight US clinical research sites from 2010 to 2014 were followed through delivery; DNAm arrays were processed in 2024, and the current analysis was conducted in 2026. Participants were nulliparous individuals with singleton pregnancies who self-identified as Black. Maternal peripheral blood DNA methylation was measured at 6 to13 weeks of gestation using the Illumina MethylationEPIC array. The primary aging metric was standardized GrimAge2 age acceleration. Principal Components versions of the Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, GrimAge, and DNAmTL clocks, and DunedinPACE, were used in additional analyses. Delivery data was abstracted from medical records in the NuMom2b study. Outcomes were gestational duration in days, based on the best obstetric estimate, adjudicated sPTB before 37 completed weeks, and SGA. Primary linear and logistic regression models adjusted for maternal age, smoking, gestational age at blood draw, and estimated blood cell composition. Secondary models added education and body mass index (BMI) as additional covariates. Fetal sex interaction effects were tested. Results: Among 931 participants (mean age = 23.46 [SD=5.33] years), 55 (5.9%) experienced sPTB. Each 1-SD higher GrimAge2 acceleration was associated with 1.32 fewer days of gestation (b = -1.32 days; 95% CI, -2.36 to -0.28; P=.01) and higher odds of sPTB (odds ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.13-2.02; P=.01). Results were slightly attenuated but remained significant for sPTB when controlling for education and BMI. Epigenetic age acceleration was not associated with SGA. Results were not significantly different by fetal sex. Conclusions and Relevance: Greater first-trimester maternal GrimAge2 acceleration was associated with shorter gestation and 51% higher odds of sPTB but was not associated with SGA among Black nulliparous participants. The association with sPTB persisted after adjustment for socioeconomic and metabolic characteristics, warranting further evaluation of whether GrimAge2 improves early-pregnancy prediction of sPTB value beyond these factors.

papers.title: Multimodal investigation of endometriosis by using LA-ICP-MS and QCL-based infrared microscopy
papers.abstract: Endometriosis affects millions of women worldwide. It is linked to severe pain and leads to high socio-economic costs. Endometriosis is characterized by the growth of tissue resembling the endometrium outside the uterus, with the cause still unclear. This study demonstrates how multimodal bioimaging methods can provide new insights into the elemental and molecular processes of endometriosis at the macroscopic level. By using multimodal bioimaging techniques, the role of trace elements (TE) and changes in molecular composition were investigated in human endometriosis biopsies and compared with TE concentrations in serum and peritoneal fluid during the disease. As an element-specific bioimaging technique, laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) was utilized to analyze the TE profile in human biopsies with high sensitivity. Additionally, a quantum cascade laser-based infrared microspectroscopy generated complementary spatial molecular information of the affected tissue. The chemometric processing of the molecular data was made by using uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP). To validate the results obtained, TE levels in body fluids were quantified by using ICP-MS and microassays. Our study demonstrates that differences in the TE profile and at the protein level, in terms of mucin expression, can be detected in lesion areas. The TE changes in the tissue differed from those in the body fluids. The presence of mucins in the lesion areas was additionally confirmed by immunohistochemistry. These results highlight the potential of imaging methods in the field of endometriosis research and offer a promising avenue for further studies.

papers.title: Health workers' and administrators' experiences of duty handover on maternity wards in public health facilities in Hoima District, Uganda: a qualitative phenomenological study
papers.abstract: Background: Duty handover is a high-risk point in the continuity of maternity care, and breakdowns in handover communication have been linked to delayed care and avoidable harm. Qualitative evidence from maternity wards in low-resource Sub-Saharan African settings is limited, and to our knowledge no study has examined handover experiences on maternity wards in Hoima District, Uganda. This study explored the experiences and challenges of health workers and administrators regarding duty handover on maternity wards in public health facilities in Hoima District, Uganda. Methods: We conducted a qualitative phenomenological study. Fifteen in-depth interviews with maternity ward health workers and five key informant interviews with administrators were carried out across six public health facilities. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed using a modified Colaizzi seven-step method. Reflexivity and bracketing were addressed through a pre-fieldwork assumptions statement and bracketing interview, a reflexive journal kept throughout data collection, and independent double-coding of a subset of transcripts. Results: Two themes were identified: duty handover practices on maternity wards, and challenges experienced by health workers during handover. Handover was inconsistent in structure, duration and adherence to protocol, and relied heavily on informal telephone communication rather than structured face-to-face reporting. Standardised tools were used in some facilities only. Participants identified time constraints and workload, inadequate training, limited resources and supervision, negative staff attitudes, and difficulty accessing patient information as key challenges, and linked communication breakdowns to delays and errors in care. Patients and families were largely not involved in handover. Conclusions: Duty handover on the maternity wards studied was inconsistent and constrained by capability-, opportunity- and motivation-related barriers operating together. Standardised and locally adapted handover tools, targeted training, stronger supervision and facility- and national-level guidance appear necessary to protect continuity of care in comparable low-resource maternity settings. Keywords: duty handover; maternity care; patient safety; qualitative research; phenomenology; Sub-Saharan Africa; Uganda

papers.title: Anaemia in pregnancy in Bangladesh by the WHO 2024 haemoglobin cut-offs: a national biomarker survey and comparison with 2011
papers.abstract: Background. Anaemia in pregnancy is linked to low birthweight, preterm birth and maternal death. Bangladesh has had no publicly documented national haemoglobin survey of pregnant women since 2011, and WHO revised its cut-offs in 2024. We estimated national prevalence under these cut-offs, described haemoglobin across gestation, and compared 2025 with 2011. Methods. We analysed venous haemoglobin from 1,933 of 2,711 eligible pregnant women in the nationally representative Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2025. We reanalysed capillary haemoglobin from 352 pregnant women in the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey 2011. Anaemia was haemoglobin below 11.0 g/dL in the first and third trimesters and below 10.5 g/dL in the second. Survey-weighted modified Poisson models estimated prevalence ratios (PR). Results. In 2025, 53.2% (95% CI 50.6 to 55.8) of pregnant women were anaemic and 22.3% (20.2 to 24.5) had moderate or severe anaemia. A single 11.0 g/dL cut-off gave 60.7%. Prevalence was 42.1% in the first trimester and 67.7% in the third. Mean haemoglobin was lowest in month 6 and only 0.23 g/dL higher in months 8 and 9 than in months 5 and 6. Prevalence was similar across wealth, education and division. It was higher in Hindu women (adjusted PR 1.27, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.45) and slightly higher in urban women (1.13, 1.02 to 1.26). Under identical rules, prevalence was 42.9% (37.1 to 48.8) in 2011 (adjusted PR for 2025, 1.33, 1.15 to 1.54; 1.29, 1.11 to 1.50 with haemoglobin rounded as in 2011). The difference was concentrated in urban women (2.36, 1.62 to 3.42) rather than rural women (1.14, 0.97 to 1.35); the interaction had p<0.001. An assay offset of 0.4 g/dL removed the national difference but not the urban one. Conclusions. About half of pregnant women in Bangladesh are anaemic, two in three by the third trimester, across all social groups. We found no evidence that anaemia has declined since 2011, and urban women appear to have lost their earlier advantage. Antenatal programmes need universal reach into late pregnancy, and surveys need harmonised haemoglobin methods.

papers.title: Effects of a standardized saffron extract (Safr'Inside™) on menopause-related symptoms: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in perimenopausal women
papers.abstract: Menopausal symptoms, which may emerge during perimenopause and include psychological, somatic, vasomotor, and sleep-related disturbances, can substantially impair women's well-being and quality of life. Saffron (Crocus sativus L.) has emerged as a promising non-hormonal nutritional approach, with potential benefits for emotional wellbeing and stress-related symptoms. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of Safr'Inside, a standardized saffron extract, in perimenopausal women. This multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial enrolled 104 healthy perimenopausal women (mean age: 45.7 {+/-} 3.7 years) receiving Safr'Inside (30 mg/day) or matched placebo for 12 weeks. Assessments were performed at baseline, 6 week, and 12 weeks. The primary outcome was change in menopausal symptom severity assessed using the Greene Climacteric Scale (GCS). Secondary outcomes included mood assessed using the Profile of Mood States (POMS), sleep quality using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and health-related quality of life using the Short Form-36(SF-36). Metabolic, endocrine, and safety parameters were also assessed. At week 12, total GCS scores decreased significantly more with Safr'Inside than with placebo, with mean reductions of 68% and 17%, respectively (p<0.0001). Improvements were already evident at week 6 and were most pronounced for psychological and somatic symptoms, including anxiety and depression. Night sweats significantly improved, while the overall vasomotor score showed a favourable trend (p=0.06). Saffron also improved negative mood, selected sleep-related outcomes and several dimensions of quality of life. Safr'Inside significantly reduced overall perimenopausal symptom burden, with benefits across psychological, somatic, mood, sleep-related, and selected vasomotor outcomes. These findings support further investigation of standardized saffron extract as a non-hormonal nutritional approach for perimenopausal symptom management.

papers.title: Opioid Analgesic Initiation During Pregnancy and the Risk of Adverse Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes: A Target Trial Emulation
papers.abstract: BackgroundWe used sequential target trial emulation (TTE) to examine associations between opioid analgesic initiation and adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes while accounting for gestational timing, time at risk, and potential confounding. MethodsUsing the Early Life Course platform, comprising linked population-based data for births in New South Wales, Australia (2013-2019), we emulated a new trial at each gestational week, comparing women who initiated a prescribed opioid analgesic with eligible non-initiators. Baseline covariates were balanced using inverse probability weighting. Weighted logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for neonatal outcomes, postpartum haemorrhage, and severe maternal morbidity. Pooled logistic regression estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for other maternal outcomes, combined across gestational weeks using fixed-effects meta-analysis. Sensitivity analyses assessed unmeasured confounding, exposure misclassification, and potential reverse causation. FindingsAmong 511,357 pregnancies, over 80% of opioid initiators received only one dispensing. Opioid initiation was not associated with increased risks of placental abruption (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.75-1.16), severe maternal morbidity (OR 1.05, 0.97-1.11), postpartum haemorrhage (OR 0.98, 0.95-1.02), low Apgar score (OR 0.99, 0.87-1.08), small for gestational age (OR 0.90, 0.85-0.95), or neonatal abstinence syndrome (OR 0.98, 0.72-1.30). Risks were elevated for PPROM (HR 1.10, 0.98-1.23), preterm birth (HR 1.26, 1.19-1.33), severe neonatal morbidity (OR 1.08, 1.02-1.17), and perinatal death (OR 1.29, 1.10-1.52). Perinatal death estimates attenuated in analyses addressing potential reverse causation. InterpretationUsing a TTE approach that accounted for gestational timing and time at risk, we found no appreciable increase in most maternal or neonatal outcomes following predominantly short-term opioid initiation. Elevated risks of preterm birth, perinatal death, and third-trimester PPROM may reflect causal effects or confounding by pregnancy-related indications. Studies using time-appropriate designs and detailed information on prescribing indications and their timing are needed to clarify these associations. Research in ContextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSWe searched the electronic databases MEDLINE (PubMed) for published articles, without language restrictions, from 1 January 2000 until 9 September 2026. The search strategy included terms for exposure (e.g. analgesic opioids), population (e.g. pregnancy and neonatal) and maternal and neonatal outcomes (e.g. preterm birth). Our search identified 10 observational studies which examined maternal and neonatal outcomes following opioid analgesic exposure during pregnancy. In these studies, prenatal opioid exposure above certain levels was consistently associated with neonatal abstinence syndrome (NAS). Beyond NAS, findings were inconsistent: some studies reported increased risks of peripartum haemorrhage, stillbirth, small for gestational age, low Apgar scores, preterm birth, and placental abruption, whereas others found no increased risk. It remains unclear whether observed associations are causal or reflect residual confounding. Methodological limitations may also have obscured associations, including immortal time bias when treatment initiation and follow-up were not aligned, and analyses that did not adequately account for gestational timing and therefore may have missed periods of greater susceptibility. As opioid analgesics are among the few options for managing pain during pregnancy, high-quality evidence on their safety is essential for informed clinical decision-making. Added value of this studyThis study applied a sequential target trial emulation framework to estimate the effects of opioid analgesic initiation during pregnancy across a broad range of maternal and neonatal outcomes, aligning eligibility, treatment initiation, and follow-up while accounting for gestational timing. Opioid initiation was not associated with appreciably increased risks of most outcomes, including placental abruption, postpartum haemorrhage, severe maternal morbidity, and low Apgar scores. A small increase was observed for severe neonatal morbidity. Relative risks increased across trimesters for preterm birth, while PPROM and perinatal death were most elevated following third-trimester initiation. These findings may reflect opioid effects, although evolving pregnancy complications that both prompt opioid treatment and independently increase outcome risk remain a plausible explanation. NAS risk was not increased overall, although estimates were higher for oxycodone and higher oral morphine equivalent (OME) exposure. Implications of all available evidenceTaken together with broader evidence showing no substantial increase in the risk of major congenital malformations or adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes, these findings are generally reassuring for short-term opioid analgesic use in pregnancy, particularly codeine. The observed signals for preterm birth, PPROM and perinatal death, should not, in isolation, deter clinically indicated use, but support existing guidance to use opioids at the lowest effective dose for the shortest necessary duration and highlight the need for further studies that can distinguish direct opioid effects from shared clinical pathways.

papers.title: Expression and Distribution of Src Kinase Lyn in the Placenta of Patients with Preeclampsia
papers.abstract: Src family kinases (SFKs) constitute a major non-receptor tyrosine kinase class that regulate processes important for pregnancy. We profiled placental SFKs to assess cell-specific expression, tissue localization, and clinical associations in early-onset preeclampsia (PE). Placental SFK transcripts were analyzed using bulk RNA sequencing discovery (GSE203507; n=15 PE, n=15 controls) and external validation (GSE114691; n=40 PE, n=21 controls) cohorts. Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing atlases mapped cell-specific expression. Computational deconvolution and causal mediation analyses were applied to bulk datasets. Findings were cross-validated by real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR; n=9 early-onset PE, n=7 controls) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Transcriptomic data showed that LYN was the sole SFK member consistently elevated in early-onset PE placentas across discovery (1.8-fold, FDR<0.01) and validation cohorts (2.2-fold, FDR<0.001). Elevation was verified by qPCR (p<0.0001) and remained significant after adjusting for clinical covariates. Placental LYN abundance correlated positively with maximum antepartum maternal systolic blood pressure (r=0.63, p<0.01). Single-cell transcriptome atlases demonstrated LYN enrichment in myeloid lineages, extravillous trophoblasts, and syncytiotrophoblast (SCT). Deconvolution and mediation analyses indicated that altered tissue composition and increased per-cell expression each accounted for approximately half of the PE-associated LYN increase. IHC localized Lyn protein to Hofbauer macrophages and the apical microvillar SCT membrane in PE placentas. We conclude that placental LYN expression is selectively elevated in early-onset PE and correlates with maternal blood pressure severity. Lyn localization to trophoblasts and placental immune cells suggests potential roles in mediating inflammation and hypoxia-associated signaling in PE pathogenesis.

papers.title: Recurrence patterns and adjuvant therapy in endometrioid early-stage endometrial cancer with a p53-abnormal pattern
papers.abstract: ObjectiveCurrent guidelines recommend different adjuvant treatment strategies for women with endometrioid early-stage endometrial cancer exhibiting a p53-abnormal pattern. We aimed to evaluate recurrence patterns and explore the clinical implications for adjuvant therapy in this population. Materials and methodsThis multicenter retrospective study included 86 patients with endometrioid, p53-abnormal, FIGO stage I-II endometrial cancer treated between 2013 and 2023 at six hospitals in the Republic of Korea. Clinicopathologic data were collected through medical record review. Progression-free survival (PFS) was estimated using the Kaplan- Meier method, and prognostic factors were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards regression models. ResultsThe 12-, 24-, and 36-month PFS rates were 91%, 78%, and 76%, respectively. Among the 16 patients who experienced recurrence, 12 (75%) had distant metastases. Adjuvant chemotherapy showed a trend toward improved PFS compared with adjuvant radiation therapy with or without chemotherapy (p=0.10). In multivariable analysis, the p53-overexpression pattern was independently associated with worse PFS compared with the p53-null pattern (HR 8.59, 95% CI 1.61-45.79, p=0.01). ConclusionGiven the poor PFS, the predominance of distant recurrence and the observed trend toward improved PFS with chemotherapy, adjuvant chemotherapy may be considered in women with endometrioid early-stage endometrial cancer exhibiting a p53-abnormal pattern. Further studies are warranted to clarify the prognostic impact of p53 abnormality subtypes.

papers.title: Menstrual symptoms and infertility odds among individuals with co-occurring endometriosis and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
papers.abstract: Structured abstractO_ST_ABSObjectiveC_ST_ABSTo study the prevalence of co-occurring endometriosis and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), estimate infertility odds, and characterize menstrual symptom profiles associated with this combined phenotype in a population cohort. DesignProspective digital cohort in the United States (US). Subjects90,714 consented participants enrolled between November 2019 and June 2025 who completed relevant surveys; a subset of 25,152 participants with menstrual cycle logs linked to monthly surveys contributed to symptom analyses. ExposureParticipants were classified by self-reported physician diagnosis into four groups: endometriosis alone, PMOS alone, co-occurring endometriosis and PMOS (endometriosis+PMOS), or neither condition (reference group). Main Outcome Measures(1) Odds of self-reported physician-diagnosed infertility (ever/never, cross-sectional), estimated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, race/ethnicity, and subjective socioeconomic status; (2) number of adverse menstrual symptoms logged per cycle, assessed using negative binomial mixed-effects models adjusted for age, race/ethnicity, and hormonal contraceptive use. ResultsAmong 90,714 participants, the mean age was 35.1 years (standard deviation: 11.6) and the majority identified as non-Hispanic White (72%). Prevalence estimates were 11% for PMOS alone, 6% for endometriosis alone, and 2% for endometriosis+PMOS. Individuals with endometriosis+PMOS more frequently reported unemployment, low socioeconomic status, active smoking, poorer subjective health, early menarche, current irregular cycles, and a broad range of comorbidities. Infertility odds were highest for endometriosis+PMOS (odds ratio: 12.49 [95% confidence interval: 11.13-13.99]), followed by PMOS alone (6.12 [5.69-6.59]) and endometriosis alone (4.31 [3.93-4.72]), with the combined effect exceeding additive expectations (relative excess risk due to interaction: 3.05 [1.65-4.46]). Individuals with endometriosis+PMOS logged 11% more symptoms per cycle than those with neither condition (incidence rate ratio: 1.11 [1.04-1.19]) and had the highest odds of logging pelvic pain, fatigue, and sleep changes, among other symptoms. ConclusionIn this large US digital cohort, co-occurring endometriosis and PMOS affected 1 in 50 participants and was associated with markedly elevated infertility odds exceeding additive expectations, and a heightened menstrual symptom burden. Several risk factors and health impacts characteristic of each condition appeared amplified in individuals with both conditions, suggesting a subgroup with compounded clinical complexity and greater care needs.

papers.title: Stage-Aware and Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting IVF Implantation
papers.abstract: Predicting implantation outcomes in vitro fertilization (IVF) is challenging because clinically relevant information becomes available at different points during treatment. In this study, we developed a stage-aware, leakage-conscious, and explainable machine-learning framework to predict implantation using a public IVF dataset. {beta}-HCG was excluded to avoid potential downstream target leakage. The data were divided into training, validation, and independent test sets. Several machine-learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest (RF), Extra Trees, XGBoost, and Hist Gradient Boosting, were optimized using stratified cross-validation. A fixed RF model was then evaluated at three stages of the IVF process, using baseline couple characteristics, gamete and fertilization variables, and embryological variables, respectively. Model performance improved as additional treatment-related information became available, with the largest improvement observed after the inclusion of embryological variables. The final RF model showed good predictive performance on the independent test set. The number of embryos was consistently identified as the most important predictor across RF, permutation, and SHAP analyses. Overall, the findings suggest that IVF implantation prediction becomes more accurate as later-stage treatment information is incorporated, particularly information related to embryological characteristics. The proposed approach also provides interpretable predictions while reducing the risk of information leakage. Further evaluation using independent clinical datasets is needed before the framework can be considered for clinical use.

papers.title: Blood lead and other metals among pregnant women in Bangladesh: national prevalence, geographic variation and household child exposure
papers.abstract: BackgroundLead crosses the placenta and harms the developing brain, and no safe level is known. Bangladesh lacks national estimates of lead exposure in pregnancy. ObjectivesWe estimated blood lead in pregnant women nationally, described where and in whom it was raised, and examined links with child lead and haemoglobin. MethodsIn the Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2025, 1,932 of 2,711 eligible pregnant women (71%) had valid venous blood results. Survey-weighted modified Poisson models estimated prevalence ratios (PR) for blood lead of 3.5 {micro}g/dL or more, an analytical cut-off. We also studied 540 households with a tested child aged 12 to 59 months. ResultsAmong tested women, geometric mean blood lead was 2.05 {micro}g/dL (95% CI 1.99 to 2.12). In all, 17.7% (15.7 to 19.9) had 3.5 {micro}g/dL or more and 7.6% (6.1 to 9.3) had 5 {micro}g/dL or more. Greater Dhaka, defined after inspecting district estimates, held 12% of pregnant women but 64% (54 to 73) of those at 5 {micro}g/dL or more. The richest quintile had a crude PR of 3.06 (2.02 to 4.63, P<0.001), attenuated to 1.09 (0.72 to 1.67, P=0.678) after adjustment for place. No clear association was seen with cosmetics, indoor smoking or nearby battery sites. A womans lead of 3.5 {micro}g/dL or more was associated with child lead of 5 {micro}g/dL or more (adjusted PR 1.50, 1.16 to 1.96, P=0.002). This cut-off identified only 23% (16 to 30) of them. ConclusionsRaised blood lead in pregnancy varied sharply by place and was highest in greater Dhaka. The crude wealth association was markedly attenuated after adjustment for place. Maternal lead was linked with child lead, but most exposed children lived with women below the cut-off. These findings support source investigation in greater Dhaka and evaluation of targeted lead assessment for women and children.

papers.title: Real-World Adaptation and External Validation of Machine-Learning Impedance Spectroscopy for Immediate Postpartum Detection of Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injuries
papers.abstract: Obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) requires immediate postpartum recognition for primary repair. Diagnosis relies primarily on clinical examination, as endoanal ultrasound (EAUS) is rarely a bedside option. Therefore, objective diagnostic assessment is most needed during the first postpartum hours. However, it is challenging to obtain the anatomically verified data needed to develop diagnostic technologies for this clinical window. We evaluated the translation of a machine-learning-assisted impedance spectroscopy model into its intended immediate postpartum setting. The model lifecycle comprised three sequential phases: V1 development using anatomically verified data from a prospective multicenter study (N=152); V2 real-world adaptation, comprising post-market data collection, retraining (N=144) to adapt to acute physiological tissue changes, and subsequent separate evaluation (N=125); and prospective external validation of V2 in an unseen cohort (N=70). During this separate evaluation, V2 achieved 89.6% accuracy. In external validation, all examinations occurred within 4 hours of birth (94.3% within the first hour). Against subsequent EAUS, V2 achieved 86.2% sensitivity, 92.7% specificity, and 90.0% overall accuracy. The V2 model was prospectively externally validated in its intended immediate-postpartum setting, supporting ML-assisted impedance spectroscopy as an objective adjunct, and not a replacement, to clinical OASI assessment. Further validation is required to confirm generalizability.

papers.title: Predictors of Preeclampsia and Pregnancy Associated Outcomes Among Pregnant Women: A Prospective Cohort Study in Selected Hospitals in Kiambu County, Kenya
papers.abstract: Abstract/SummaryPreeclampsia is a multisystem hypertensive disorder of pregnancy that emerges after 20 weeks of gestation, and remains a leading cause of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality globally, yet evidence on its predictors and outcomes in Kenya remains limited. This prospective cohort study compared pregnant women with and without preeclampsia who attended selected hospitals in Kiambu County, to determine the predictors of preeclampsia and its associated maternal and neonatal outcomes. The results indicated a very strong statistical association between preeclampsia and the following i.e parity, time taken to reach the hospital, hypertension and diabetes mellitus (p-value <0.001) and religion (p-value <0.013). Women with preeclampsia had nearly twice the risk and six times the odds of delivering low-birth-weight infants compared with women without preeclampsia (RR = 1.97; OR = 6.25). A strong statistically significant association was observed between multiparity and prematurity (RR = 5.3, OR = 8.4, p < 0.001). Multiparous women with preeclampsia had approximately 5.3 times the risk and 8.4 times the odds of experiencing a premature birth compared with women without preeclampsia. In conclusion preeclampsia significantly increased adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, highlighting the need for early high-risk pregnancies identification and strengthened antenatal care to improve both maternal and neonatal outcomes.

papers.title: Effect of the WHO Labour Care Guide Implementation on Maternal and Newborn Outcomes in Selected Referral Hospitals of Zambia: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis
papers.abstract: BackgroundDespite being originally developed to support labour monitoring in low-resource and rural settings, the partograph has remained the standard tool for labour management and continues to be used by obstetricians and midwives across diverse settings worldwide. However, inappropriate use and non-use of the partograph persist and have been associated with increased odds of adverse perinatal outcomes, including perinatal death. To address these limitations, the World Health Organization introduced the Labour Care Guide in 2020 as a comprehensive tool to standardise and improve the quality of care during childbirth. Henceforth, some countries such as Rwanda and Uganda have since implemented its use. This study aimed to assess the effect of WHO Labour Care Guide implementation, compared with the traditional partograph, on selected maternal and perinatal outcomes across participating facilities. MethodsThis was a quasi-experimental implementation study conducted in selected referral hospitals in Zambia, comparing maternal and perinatal outcomes before and after implementation of the WHO Labour Care Guide. Facilities were grouped into implementation and comparison sites. Routine HMIS/DHIS2 data were used to assess selected outcomes across the pre- and post-implementation periods. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise outcome trends, while a difference-in-differences analytical approach was applied using Stata version 18 to compare changes over time between implementation and comparison sites. ResultsThe analysis included 12 hospitals, 192 facility-month observations, 89,122 total births, and 87,004 live births. Overall, the stillbirth rate was 23.8 per 1,000 total births, birth asphyxia rate was 40.1 per 1,000 live births, caesarean section rate was 34.6 per 100 live births, low-birthweight rate was 168.6 per 1,000 live births, and maternal mortality ratio was 313.8 per 100,000 live births. The implementation sites reporting higher birth asphyxia rates (42.7 versus 38.0 per 1,000 live births). Difference-in-differences analysis showed no statistically significant effect of LCG implementation on stillbirths, IRR 1.07 (95% CI: 0.69-1.67, p=0.752); fresh stillbirths, IRR 1.23 (95% CI: 0.74-2.05, p=0.431); birth asphyxia, IRR 0.65 (95% CI: 0.34-1.27, p=0.207); or caesarean section, IRR 1.02 (95% CI: 0.80-1.30, p=0.892). ConclusionImplementation of the WHO Labour Care Guide was not associated with statistically significant changes in stillbirths, fresh stillbirths, birth asphyxia, or caesarean section rates during the study period. Despite the higher birth asphyxia rates in the implementation sites the difference remained statistically not significant. Scale-up of the LCG should be accompanied by sustained training, mentorship, audit and feedback, and strengthening of emergency obstetric and newborn care systems.

papers.title: Pyelonephritis is associated with persistent alterations in immune-stromal and vascular programs in the human placenta
papers.abstract: Maternal systemic infection during pregnancy is associated with placental dysfunction even when pathogens do not directly invade the placenta, but the cellular pathways linking antecedent infection to persistent placental alterations remain poorly defined. Here we used spatial transcriptomics to resolve trophoblast-, fetal endothelial, and Hofbauer cell-enriched niches in placentas collected at term after clinical recovery from antepartum pyelonephritis. We profiled 168 spatially defined areas from 14 placentas and integrated transcriptional findings with blinded histopathology and quantitative extracellular matrix analysis. Pyelonephritis was associated with strikingly compartment-specific transcriptional responses. Hofbauer cell-enriched niches showed the most extensive alterations, with coordinated enrichment of extracellular matrix remodeling and vascular developmental programs, including increased ELN expression (log2FC = 0.84, FDR = 0.033) and increased expression of genes governing collagen deposition, elastic-fiber assembly, matrix maturation and turnover. Quantitative analysis of 1,790 fetal vessels independently identified altered perivascular matrix composition, with Hofbauer cell-enriched ELN expression correlating with greater perivascular elastin content ({rho} = 0.67, P = 0.008). Fetal endothelial-enriched regions exhibited complementary alterations in vascular remodeling and endothelial identity, including increased PLAC8 (log2FC = 1.36, FDR = 0.047), whereas trophoblast-enriched regions showed little detectable transcriptional response. Histopathology further demonstrated increased lesions associated with maternal vascular malperfusion and perivillous fibrin deposition. Together, these findings identify the villous immune-stromal-vascular microenvironment as a persistent site of placental remodeling following maternal infection and suggest that clinical recovery from maternal illness may not coincide with normalization of placental biology.

papers.title: Universal Screening with a Glucose Challenge Test to Predict Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in a Diverse Population: A Retrospective Cohort Study
papers.abstract: IntroductionGestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with significant maternal and neonatal morbidity. Screening strategies vary internationally and the diagnostic performance of the 50g glucose challenge test (50g GCT) as a universal screening tool remains uncertain across diverse populations. Research design and methodsThis retrospective cohort study included 18,213 singleton pregnancies at a London tertiary hospital between 2010 and 2023. Women routinely underwent the universal two-step GDM screening pathway: a 50g GCT at 24-32 weeks gestation, followed by a diagnostic 75-g oral glucose tolerance test if the 50g GCT result was [≥]7.8 mmol/L. We evaluated the use of universal two-step screening in detecting GDM, how its prevalence varies with maternal characteristics, including ethnicity, body mass index, age, and in those who would not have been included in risk factor-indicated screening, and the association between the 50g GCT and adverse outcomes. Results2,015 women had an abnormal GCT, and 406 (20.1%) had an abnormal 75g OGTT, with GDM diagnosed at 24-28 weeks. We also found 87 women, despite a normal GCT and/or normal OGTT, developed late-onset GDM. The overall prevalence of GDM was 4.4% (810/18,213). Universal screening will therefore identify a significant number of GDM cases, notably including those in a low-risk cohort who would not have been screened using a risk factor-based approach. When we examined glucose as a continuous variable, there was an association between increasing 50g GCT values and adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. ConclusionUniversal screening with a GCT is a feasible and safe approach and addresses a significant health disparity gap, in that women without risk factors are screened and may be diagnosed with GDM. Given the long-term cardiometabolic implications of GDM, pregnancy diagnosis is important to allow for longer-term targeting of cardiometabolic risk factors to improve long-term health screening for type 2 diabetes and obesity. Key messagesO_ST_ABSWhat is already known on this topicC_ST_ABSO_LIGestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with maternal and neonatal morbidity, which is substantially reduced with early recognition and management. C_LIO_LIGDM screening approaches vary substantially in efficiency, diagnostic accuracy, and resource use. Universal screening with a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (75g OGTT) is resource-intensive, yet risk factor-based screening alone risks missing GDM in women without recognised risk factors. C_LIO_LIThe recurrence risk of GDM is up to 41.3%, and women with GDM are more likely to develop type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disorders; therefore, diagnosis of GDM is important to identify and intervene in those women who are at higher risk. C_LIO_LIGDM is associated with increased offspring adiposity and childhood obesity, impaired glucose metabolism and a substantially elevated long-term risk of prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, as well as a broader adverse cardiometabolic profile. C_LI What this study addsO_LIUniversal screening detected GDM in women who may not have been offered screening based on risk factors. C_LIO_LIAround 1/3 of GDM cases detected in this population were diagnosed later in pregnancy following negative GCT and/or negative OGTT. C_LIO_LIThe relationship between maternal glycaemia and adverse pregnancy outcomes is continuous across GCT glucose levels, with risk increasing with increased glucose levels. C_LI How this study might affect research, practice or policyO_LIFurther research is needed to investigate how a universal screening approach in diagnosing GDM addresses longer-term cardiometabolic health. C_LIO_LIVariation in the predictive value of a GCT for GDM by maternal characteristics should be considered when evaluating and optimising any universal screening strategy. C_LIO_LIA GCT population could form part of a hybrid GDM screening strategy where high-risk women proceed directly to 75g OGTT and women considered at low risk of GDM benefit from screening by GCT. papers.title: Contribution of maternal and fetal genetics to fetal weight throughout pregnancy and at birth
papers.abstract: BackgroundBoth fetal and maternal genomes contribute to birthweight, but the timing and relative magnitude of their effects during gestation remain unclear. Polygenic risk scores (PRSs), constructed from genome-wide association studies (GWAS), capture the cumulative influence of common birthweight-associated variants to quantify genetic predisposition to fetal growth. We constructed fetal and maternal PRSs for birthweight in two UK birth cohorts, the Pregnancy Outcome Prediction Study (POPS) and Born in Bradford (BiB), to evaluate their associations with estimated fetal weight (EFW) throughout pregnancy and with birthweight at delivery. We also investigated whether PRSs could improve risk stratification of infants born below the 10th centile by distinguishing those with pathological intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) from those who are constitutionally small-for-gestational-age (SGA). MethodsIn POPS and BiB, we used LDpred2-auto to estimate PRSs based on the largest available maternal and fetal GWAS for birthweight. We longitudinally assessed EFW associations with PRSs using linear mixed effects models in POPS and BiB. We evaluated birthweight associations with PRSs using linear models, where birthweight was adjusted for gestational age and fetal sex. We estimated R2 and conducted variance decomposition analyses for all models. Genetically-predicted birthweights were estimated from joint models of fetal and maternal PRSs plus ten genetic principal components (PCs). BiB analyses were conducted separately for genetically-inferred European (EUR) and South Asian (SAS) ancestry. ResultsWhile PRSfetus was significantly associated with EFW at baseline ([~]22 weeks gestation) across cohorts, PRSmother was not. Both the interaction of PRSfetus and PRSmother with gestational age (GA) were significantly associated with EFW. The effect of PRSmother on EFW increased more quickly across gestation than the effect of PRSfetus in POPS, but this finding was not replicated in BiB. Jointly, fetal and maternal polygenic risk explained 4% of variance in EFW in POPS and 1% in BiB-EUR. In POPS, fetal and maternal PRSs showed independent contributions to EFW variance of 3% and 0.5%, respectively. Joint and univariable linear models showed significant positive associations of PRSfetus and PRSmother with observed birthweight. In POPS, PRSfetus and PRSmother accounted for [~]10% and [~]4% of variance in birthweight over covariates alone, respectively, which was replicated in BiB-EUR. Maternal and fetal genetic effects jointly explained 11% of birthweight variance in POPS, similar to BiB-EUR, at 12%; however, the variance explained was reduced by half in BiB-SAS, at 6%. Among POPS babies born <10th birthweight centile, the magnitude of the difference between observed and genetically-predicted birthweight was greater in the group judged clinically to be IUGR vs. SGA (p=0.008; point estimate=0.29, 95%CI: 0.12, 0.47). ConclusionsMaternal and fetal PRSs jointly account for [~]11-12% of birthweight variance in European ancestry groups, but much less in a South Asian cohort. In POPS, the effect of birthweight-associated SNPs on estimated fetal weight increases more rapidly across pregnancy for maternal than for fetal genetic effects. Deviation from genetically-predicted birthweight may be a useful metric to help distinguish growth-restricted from constitutionally small babies. O_LITweetable statement: Fetal and maternal genetics both influence fetal growth across gestation. Growth-restricted babies have greater differences between their genetically-predicted and observed birthweights compared to those who are constitutionally small.
